summary.text: Fast ice is sea or lake ice held in place because it is attached to the coastline, to the sea floor along shoals, or to grounded icebergs.
Unlike drifting pack ice, it does not move with currents and winds, and it forms either by freezing in place or by drifting pieces freezing onto an anchor.
Its width usually changes with the seasons and ranges from a few meters to several hundred kilometers, depending on ice thickness and the shape of the sea floor and islands.

facts.label: Width range
facts.value: A few meters to several hundred kilometers

items.prompt: A strong wind blows across a frozen bay for two days. What happens to the sheet of ice that is frozen to the shoreline?

options.label: It drifts out to sea with the wind
It slides along with the current

items.explain: Ice attached to the coast does not move with winds and currents, unlike drifting pack ice.

items.prompt: In the name "fast ice", what does the word "fast" refer to?

options.label: It is held fixed to the coast or seabed
It moves faster than other sea ice
It melts quickly when summer comes

items.explain: "Fast" means fastened: the ice is anchored to the coastline, shoals, or grounded icebergs.

items.prompt: Along one coast the shelf drops away steeply and there are no islands. What can stop any shore-anchored ice from forming there?

options.label: The saltiness of the deep water
The rise and fall of the tides

items.explain: In some coastal areas with an abrupt shelf and no islands, such as off Hokkaidō, tides prevent fast ice from forming.

items.prompt: In which seas does shore-anchored ice reach into deeper water?

options.label: Both reach the same 10 m depth

items.explain: In Arctic seas the zone extends to about 20 m deep, while in Subarctic seas it reaches about 10 m.

items.prompt: Out at sea, moving pack ice grinds along the edge of ice that is frozen in place. What may form along that boundary?
items.explain: The limit between fast ice and drifting pack ice may in places coincide with a shear ridge.

items.prompt: On a tidal shore, water left behind by each falling tide freezes again and again into a band of ice at the beach. What separates this band from the rest of the shore-anchored ice?
items.explain: This band is the ice foot, formed by repeated freezing between ebb tides and cut off from the rest of the fast ice by tidal cracks.
